title: Understanding Cross-Entropy Loss
text: Cross-entropy loss is a measure of the difference between two probability distributions. In binary classification, it is used to measure the difference between the true labels and the predicted probabilities.

title: Formula for Cross-Entropy Loss
text: The cross-entropy loss for a single data point is given by:\n- For true label 1: -log(predicted probability)\n- For true label 0: -log(1-predicted probability)

title: Calculate Individual Losses
text:
Calculate the cross-entropy loss for each data point using the formula:
- For the first data point (true label $$0$$, predicted probability $$0.1)$$: $$-\ln\left(1-0.1ight)$$
- For the second data point (true label $$0$$, predicted probability $$0.6)$$: $$-\ln\left(1-0.6ight)$$
- For the third data point (true label $$1$$, predicted probability $$0.9)$$: $$-\ln\left(0.9ight)$$

title: Sum the Losses
text: Add the individual cross-entropy losses to get the total loss.
